notes:
Passed on the fake backend (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware was attached and no hardware run is claimed. The upstream Isaac-Drone-Racer-v0 environment was not run: it needs Isaac Sim 4.5.0 (README.md:7), Isaac Lab v2.1.0 (README.md:44-48) and a GPU. The registered entry point is the external isaaclab.envs:ManagerBasedRLEnv (tasks/drone_racer/__init__.py:15), so the card's confirmed entry symbol DroneRacerEnvCfg is native and G7 reports five MAYBE_ABSENT warnings for the Gymnasium environment interface inherited from a base outside the clone. The fake backend (fake.py) is a pure Python stand-in: it models the four rotor commands, the total vertical thrust, the 10 ms step, the 20 s time limit, the 20 m flyaway and a 20-value policy observation inferred from the six concatenated terms of the configuration, but not the rigid-body attitude dynamics, the body moments, aerodynamic drag, contacts, the gate-passing logic or the reward (always 0.0), and it was never compared with the upstream environment. The sim backend (gymnasium.make of the registered environment) was not run. The 4096 parallel environments of the configuration are not mirrored: the fake is single-instance. Expected warnings, listed in the last check: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (bookkeeping, no native call), five G7.MAYBE_ABSENT for action_space, observation_space, reset, step and close, and four G8.NO_UNIT for the integer or derived inputs the bridge exposes. Only catalogue classes cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used, so there are no catalogue requests and no site-limits overlay. gate.digest is the digest the check printed (the report without its clock); check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
